The objective of this work is to evaluate the performance of the FFF and FGF techniques in terms of technical and economical dimensions at the desktop 3D printing scale. Recycled and virgin polylactic acid material was studied by using five different types of recycling feedstocks: commercial filament, pellets, distributed filament, distributed pellets, and shredded waste. The results showed that the mechanical properties from the FGF technique using same configurations showed no statistical differences to FFF samples.

title: Distributed Recycling VIa Additive Manufacturing
text:
Here a presentation of the research on distributed recycling.
Emily and I had the pleasure of presenting to the 2024 cohort of LDI Summer Undergraduate Mentored Research Program (SUMR). The materials for this interactive presentation were adapted from the Urban Institute’s series of Do No Harm guides, which focus on how to incorporate principles of equity into data collection, visualization, and communication. We concluded our talk by playing a game with the Scholars, encouraging them to use what they took away from the presentation to identify areas for improvement in a series of visualizations taken from published dashboards, papers, and other sources.

title: Fabio A. Cruz Sanchez
text:
I work specifically at the Research team on innovation process -ERPI- Laboratory and teach at the National School in Industrial Systems Engineering and Innovation -ENSGSI School- at Nancy - France.
My research is developed at the Lorraine Fab Living Lab Plateform on projects related to the concept of Distributed recycling for circular economy perspectives valuing the partnership between open source tools, social innovation spaces, holistic indicators as a way to put in place sustainability approaches for a post-growth scenarios.
Learn more about my research →

title: Fabio A. Cruz Sanchez
text:
Hey, I’m happy you’re here

I work at the Université de Lorraine in France in topics related to the mechanical and innovation engineering.
The objet of my research is the concept of distributed recycling process. The idea is to better understand the limits of this approach as a short/medium strategy of the plastic waste problem. I am very interested to work with fantastic people to make a holistic analysis of this topic, by doing research from technical, logistical and systemic evaluation.
Learn more about my research interests in publications.
Get in touch by sending me a note!

title: Fabio A. Cruz Sanchez
text:
About me


Mechanical engineer that turned into innovation science
I am learning about the role of Engineering from a perspective of the sustainability sciences. I am curious on the role of history and philosophy may have in a world where the critical thinking is becoming a rare asset. I am optimist in the value of education on engineering for the societal challenges of our world.
